subject: Throughput regression, proposed credit, and contract amendment
messages:
From: Samira Khan <samira.khan@aurora.ai>
To: support@redwood.ai
Cc: t.ellis@aurora.ai
Date: Wed, 5 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Sustained throughput regression impacting nightly batch windows (URGENT)

Hi Redwood team,

We saw a dramatic throughput regression starting late on May 3rd and persisting through May 4th. Over our nightly ingest windows the p50 token throughput dropped by ~45% and error rates (502/504) increased to ~3.8% for the 00:00-06:00 UTC window. This blew past our operational tolerance and caused Aurora's downstream enrichment jobs to miss an SLA to our end customers.

We've attached a short CSV with sampled request IDs and the Grafana panel link for the window. The impact has immediate commercial implications for Aurora; our ops and product teams are preparing a formal incident report and need a remediation and credit proposal from Redwood before we escalate to our procurement/finance team.

Please confirm:
- What root cause analysis steps are you running?
- Proposed interim mitigations to prevent reoccurrence during our nightly windows next week.
- Preliminary credit / billing remediation for the May month based on your SLA.

We need something documented by EOD PT tomorrow (May 6) to avoid starting a formal third-party review.

Thanks,
Samira Khan
Head of Platform Reliability
Aurora Systems

Attachment: aurora_error_summary_may04.csv (CSV, 42KB)

From: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.ai>
To: Samira Khan <samira.khan@aurora.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 5 May 2027 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Sustained throughput regression impacting nightly batch windows (URGENT)

Samira — thank you for the detailed report and the CSV. I’m very sorry for the disruption. I’ve looped in Ben (AE), Monica (CS) and Vivek (Eng leader) so we can coordinate a single response and a remediation + commercial proposal.

Quick answers:
- Root cause: preliminary telemetry points at a suboptimal kernel path on the batch router for sequences > 1,024 tokens under burst load; Vivek’s team is running a replay on the production snapshots now.
- Interim mitigation: we can pinned-route Aurora traffic to a stable legacy runtime pool for the next 72 hours while we validate the fix; this will reduce the variance in throughput while we complete the patch.
- Credit: I will send a preliminary credit calc tomorrow morning once we agree internally on the SLA interpretation (the contract has both uptime and throughput SLO clauses).

Proposed next steps:
1) Vivek to confirm the replay results by EOD PST today.
2) Implement pinned routing for Aurora by 02:00 UTC May 6 (we can provide a runbook).
3) Ben/Monica + Samira to sync on exact invoice(s) to apply any credit against and procurement contact.
4) I’ll draft a credit note + a proposed contract amendment (throughput SLO language + remediation steps) and circulate for review by May 9.

If Aurora wants an executive-level call to review the commercial remedy, I can join with our Head of Revenue.

— Priya Natarajan
Director, Account Strategy
Redwood Inference

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 5 May 2027 15:28:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Sustained throughput regression impacting nightly batch windows (URGENT)

Quick update from the engineering replay: the regression reproduces when the router selects the optimized kernel for long-context batching under a specific batch size distribution that Aurora hit during the May 3 peak. Patch is small — a selector fallback — and we validated it in staging.

I recommend we:
- Roll the selector-fallback to Canary in production tonight (May 5 23:00 UTC).
- Enable pinned routing to the legacy pool for Aurora for 72 hours during nightly windows.

If Canary looks stable, we can promote the change to all pools within 48 hours. I’ll coordinate with SRE on the rollout.

Vivek
VP Engineering, Serving Runtime

On Wed, May 5, 2027 at 10:05 AM Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Samira — thank you for the detailed report and the CSV. I’m very sorry for the disruption. I’ve looped in Ben (AE), Monica (CS) and Vivek (Eng leader) so we can coordinate a single response and a remediation + commercial proposal.

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 6 May 2027 08:42:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Sustained throughput regression impacting nightly batch windows (URGENT)

Notes on commercial framing:
- Contract SLA excerpt: "Service availability or throughput below the agreed SLO entitles Customer to a service credit calculated as a percentage of monthly recurring charges corresponding to the impacted service tier." We need to be conservative, factual, and propose a number that can be approved by finance.
- Proposed preliminary credit: 10% of May’s Redwood service invoice for Aurora (pro-rated to the impacted window) — this maps to ~$42,500 based on last month’s MRR and the impacted token volumes.
- Suggestion: offer the credit as a one-time invoice adjustment AND open a 6-month amendment that adds explicit throughput SLO language plus an automatic escalation path (canary routing, reserved burst lanes). That helps Aurora avoid future outages and reduces their churn risk.

I’ve prepared a short credit calc (attached) and an amendment redline. If Priya is good with the numbers, we should push these to Aurora and let legal start a quick review.

Ben Carter
Account Executive, Strategic Accounts
Attachment: credit_calculation_draft.pdf

From: Tom Ellis <t.ellis@aurora.ai>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.ai>
Cc: Samira Khan <samira.khan@aurora.ai>, procurement@aurora.ai
Date: Fri, 7 May 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Sustained throughput regression impacting nightly batch windows (URGENT)

Priya — thanks for the quick coordination and Vivek/Ben’s notes. Aurora appreciates the proposed mitigation plan. Two asks from procurement/legal side:
1) We need a formal credit statement that we can attach to our May invoice reconciliation. Please include: calculation, invoice references, and whether this will be applied as a credit or a refund.
2) For the amendment: procurement needs a redline and a short summary of the new throughput SLO triggers and remedies. Legal will need ~5 business days to review once we have the drafts.

If Redwood can send the credit note + redline by Monday May 9 EOD PT, procurement can commit to an expedited review. We also want to schedule an exec call (Aurora CTO + Aurora CFO) to ensure alignment on scope of amendment and long-term SLA guarantees; ideally next week.

— Tom
Director, Procurement
Aurora Systems

From: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Ellis <t.ellis@aurora.ai>, Samira Khan <samira.khan@aurora.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 9 May 2027 14:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Sustained throughput regression impacting nightly batch windows (URGENT)

Tom/Samira — attached is the formal credit calculation and a redlined amendment draft for Aurora’s review. Summary:
- Credit: one-time invoice credit of $42,500 applied to May 2027 invoice AUR-INV-2027-05 (we will issue a credit note, not a cash refund, unless Aurora requests otherwise).
- Amendment: adds a "Throughput SLO" clause with explicit triggers (sustained throughput < 70% of committed capacity for a 4-hour rolling window), remediation steps, and automatic escalation to reserved routing within 60 minutes of trigger.

Links / artifacts:
- Credit calculation PDF: https://drive.redwood.com/agreements/AUR-CREDIT-2027
- Amendment redline: https://drive.redwood.com/agreements/AUR-AMD-2027

Next steps I propose:
1) Aurora legal/procurement does a 5-business-day review once you acknowledge receipt.
2) Schedule an exec-level call (Aurora CTO + CFO; Redwood Head of Revenue + Redwood CFO) — availability: Wed May 11 16:00-17:00 PT or Thu May 12 09:00-10:00 PT.
3) We will implement the pinned routing and the selector-fallback Canary tonight; I’ll confirm when the routing is active.

Looking forward to closing this quickly.

— Priya Natarajan
Director, Account Strategy
Redwood Inference
Attachment: amendment_redline_v1.docx (DOCX, 18KB); credit_calculation_draft.pdf (PDF, 12KB)
